subject.title: Adding ACP agent to agents.list silently hijacks all routing from implicit main agent

question: Should OpenClaw preserve the documented first-entry default while adding warnings/doctor guidance, or should non-empty `agents.list` require an explicit default before routing changes take effect?
rationale: The source-reproducible behavior is real, but every fix changes default-agent routing, upgrade expectations, and security posture for existing multi-agent users.

options.title: Warn And Guide
options.body: Keep first-entry compatibility for existing configs, but add warnings or doctor guidance when adding an agent would displace an existing implicit `main` state.

options.title: Require Explicit Default
options.body: Make non-empty `agents.list` invalid or blocked until an operator marks a default, with migration and docs for existing first-entry deployments.

options.title: Document Only
options.body: Keep current behavior as the product contract and improve docs/workaround wording without changing runtime or config tooling.

recommendation.title: Warn And Guide
recommendation.body: Keep first-entry compatibility for existing configs, but add warnings or doctor guidance when adding an agent would displace an existing implicit `main` state.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent ownership signals on agent-scope extraction and merged current config/routing ownership changes.
